parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment mentions "the experiments for the ablation study" and "the one about the rank," but it does not point to any specific section, table, or figure in the paper. The authors would have to make an educated guess about which part is being referenced, so the comment cannot be considered fully grounded; at best, authors can roughly infer the target area without precisely identifying it. On the other hand, the comment does clearly specify what needs to be addressed: more details on how the comparison experiment with the traditional low rank constraint was conducted. This satisfies the specificity requirement of clearly stating what should be added. However, since the grounding dimension only reaches the level where authors cannot confidently determine which part is being addressed while the specificity requirement is met, the comment corresponds to the rubric level where the part cannot be confidently identified but what needs to be addressed is clear, rather than the top level requiring both explicit grounding and specificity.
